subject: Post-demo: batching & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@retailai.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: batching & pricing follow-up

Thanks again for your time this morning, Alex — great conversation and appreciate the detailed walkthrough of RetailAI's inference patterns. Quick recap + asks so we can put together a tailored pricing + technical recommendation: 

Recap
- Primary workload: user-facing summarization + short-generation for product pages. Lots of short requests (average prompt ~120 tokens, completion ~40 tokens) with a small percent of longer analytic jobs.
- Current infra: prototype on managed endpoints; latency target 200–300ms p95 for interactive flows.
- Key constraints: cost sensitivity, predictable monthly spend, and data isolation for some PII flows.

Asks (so we can refine unit economics + batching assumptions)
1) Current monthly token volume (approx): total input+output tokens per month and expected growth over next 6–12 months.
2) Target budget range (monthly) for the initial production rollout (range is fine).
3) Desired unit economics target (e.g., $/1M tokens target) or equivalently what pricing makes switching compelling.
4) Concurrency & workload shape: typical sustained concurrency and spike behavior (users/time of day). Also confirm whether continuous batching for many small requests is acceptable versus strict single-request low-latency requirements.

Attachments: redwood-dma-1pager.pdf (product one-pager), initial-pricing-estimate.xlsx (placeholder estimate we can refine after you share volumes).

Next steps
- If you can share the numbers above, we’ll run a quick cost model (with continuous batching assumptions) and propose a recommended model/config (quantization, batching window, and routing policy) + an updated pricing sheet.
- I’ll also loop in Camila for the deeper batching/concurrency recommendations once we have volumes.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0132

On Tue, Mar 18, 2027 at 08:45 AM Alex Kim <alex@retailai.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo this morning — very helpful. I added a few notes inline.

From: Alex Kim <alex@retailai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: batching & pricing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below to help you model: 

1) Current monthly token volume: roughly 250,000,000 tokens/month (combined input + output). We are projecting ~30% QoQ growth as we onboard additional product pages and marketing traffic.
2) Target budget: for Phase 1 production we'd be comfortable in the $10k–$15k/month band (flexible for first 3 months if unit economics look good).
3) Target unit economics: we'd love to get to ~$50 / 1M tokens or better. At that price, scaling is much easier to justify internally.
4) Concurrency & workload shape: steady low concurrency most of the day (avg ~10 concurrent requests), with short spikes up to ~50 concurrent during peak campaigns. Most requests are small (see avg tokens above). Continuous batching is OK as long as p95 stays under ~350ms for interactive flows — we care about perceived latency more than single-request micro latency.

We reviewed your one-pager and the initial pricing file — looks reasonable as a starting point. Happy to hop on a follow-up with Camila to dive into batching details.

—Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Product, RetailAI
alex@retailai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@retailai.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: batching & pricing follow-up

Appreciate the quick details, Alex — this is exactly what we need to run a meaningful model. A few quick notes + initial sizing assumptions we’ll use: 

Assumptions (will refine once we have traffic distribution + 95th percentile sizes):
- Monthly tokens: 250M (as you reported)
- Avg request size: prompt 120 tokens / completion 40 tokens (160 tokens total per request)
- Requests per month estimate: ~1.56M requests (250M tokens / 160 tokens per request)
- Typical concurrency: average 10, spikes to 50 — we’ll size for sustained 15 with headroom for spikes via autoscale/burst.
- Continuous batching profile: many small requests arriving across threads, so continuous-batching (micro-batch window ~5–15ms, batching across connections) reduces per-token cost significantly vs no batching. We will assume a conservative batching efficiency of ~2.5x token throughput improvement in cost (varies by model & quantization).

Preliminary unit-econ estimate (very rough):
- If we target $50 / 1M tokens: 250M tokens => $12,500/month (baseline)
- With continuous batching and quantization recommendations we believe we can get effective infra cost reduction that lets us offer a public-facing price in the $40–55 / 1M tokens range depending on model selection and SLA.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Camila and I will run a detailed cost model using the 250M tokens and your concurrency profile and share an updated pricing sheet with two scenarios: (a) conservative batching (1.8x efficiency) and (b) optimistic batching (3x efficiency).
2) If the numbers look good, we’ll schedule a follow-up technical call (30–45m) to review batching windows, latency tradeoffs, and recommended model variant.
3) I’ll also prepare a mutual action plan and a draft quote (DocuSign-ready) tied to a 3-month pilot.

Can you confirm the 250M number is total input+output and whether there are any regulatory regions we should consider for isolating traffic?

Thanks — I’ll aim to have the updated pricing scenarios to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: next steps for RetailAI pricing/modeling

Looping in Aditya to run the batching & infra model. Plan:
- Aditya to run two scenarios (conservative 1.8x, optimistic 3x) and produce per-1M-token cost + recommended model variant and quant/kv cache settings.
- I’ll prepare a short slide (1–2 slides) explaining continuous-batching tradeoffs and a one-slide summary for the customer showing expected p95 latency under each scenario.
- Marissa to send the updated pricing sheet + MAP and draft DocuSign after we confirm numbers.

If either of you need anything else from Alex (e.g., traffic histogram by hour or percent long tail >800 tokens), tell me and I’ll request it.

-Camila
